text:
Marta G: hey team, bringing up a new quantized llama-variant and seeing streaming stops mid-sentence. looks like stop-seq matched a subtoken fragment
Ashok R: can you paste the stream logs? is this on dedicated or hosted?
Marta G: hosted for now, tiny repro: prompt 'Human: Tell me a story about a cat' and stop set to ['\nAssistant:'] but stream ends right after 'A cat climbed' (truncated)
Marta G: log snippet: ```STREAM OUT: token_ids=[1543, 6, 999, 234] decoded='A cat climbed' meta=... STOP_CHECK: comparing tail bytes 'ĠAssistant' vs '\nAssistant:' -> false STOP_CHECK: comparing token-level match -> matched partial subtoken -> emit STOP```
Liam: ah this smells like HF tokenizer split: stop string spans token boundary, the streaming stop matcher is greedy on token-substring instead of full decoded text
Kai: also saw config.json during hf->redwood conversion had eos_token set to 1 (generic) while tokenizer uses '' as special token -> mismatch when we try to detect EOS ids
Ashok R: iirc our converter (tools/hf_to_rw.py) does `eos_id = config.get('eos_token_id')` and populates `_eos_tokens` from that id only. if tokenizer was trained with added special token '<EOS_H>' it won't match unless we map special_tokens_map -> id
Marta G: here's the minimal failing case i used: ```python
# in repro
stop = ['\nAssistant:']
resp = client.generate(model='quant-llama-v1', prompt=prompt, stream=True, stop=stop)
for chunk in resp:
  print(chunk.text, end='')
# result ends early
```
Liam: temporary workaround: use string-based post-filtering on full decoded chunks rather than token-id matching during stream. i added a small buffer that waits for whitespace or punctuation after a potential match before firing stop. seems to reduce false positives
Kai: that helps, but for correctness we should fix three layers: 1) conversion must import tokenizer.special_tokens_map and set eos_token_id(s) properly, 2) streaming stop matcher should operate on decoded text suffix (longest-first) and require boundary check, 3) chat template/system prompts must not include literal special tokens like '<EOS>' unless intentionally part of token set
Marta G: opened a PR to map special tokens: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3456 (draft). converter now does `tokenizer.add_special_tokens(mapping)` and sets config.eos_token_ids to list if provided.
Ashok R: i pushed a change to streaming matcher: compare decoded suffixes in raw UTF-8, prefer longest match, and only accept match if next char is whitespace or punctuation or end-of-stream. small perf cost but acceptable for host path. commit 1f4b2c
Marta G: tests: added unit tests that simulate subtoken splits (e.g., 'Assistant' -> ['ĠAss', 'istant']) and asserts no early stop until full string present. tests pass locally for quant-llama-v1
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled to staging at 2026-03-18T16:00 UTC by @Liam :rocket:
Liam: after deploy to staging i ran 200 prompt randomization runs. failure rate went from 8.2% -> 0.5% on the stop-seq truncation metric. still seeing rare cases when stop token includes punctuation glued to word (e.g., 'Assistant:') — tweak made to normalize stop strings by stripping trailing colons in matcher
Kai: also note: quantized models can change subtokenization slightly if conversion used SentencePiece vs BPE mapping. we added a QA step to validate that tokenizer.encode(stop)[-len(stop_bytes):] equals expected bytes; otherwise warn
Marta G: plan: push converter fix + streaming matcher to main, run canary on 10% hosted traffic tomorrow, monitor stop-regression dashboard (new panel in Optimize). if green, ramp. thanks all :clap:
Ashok R: nice detective work. follow-up items: add an alert when stop-seq match rate spikes and record decoded suffix distributions for offline analysis
Liam: noted, i'll add alert and a small eval comparing HF decode vs Redwood decode for new models. will post results here once canary runs
Marta G: sweet. saved repro in /mnt/project/qa/stopseq-repro and added steps to the onboarding checklist. closing thread once canary passes :white_check_mark:
